inventory.text: Career Seekers Launch a Career in Healthcare as a Certified Nurse Assistant Becoming a Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) gets you started working in healthcare while providing opportunities to continue advancing in your career for more professional and personal growth. Start Your New Career Find a Training Provider Where are you in your career journey I am considering a new career in healthcare Learn About CNAs and Long-Term Care I am looking for a CNA traning Find a Training Provider Near You I am looking to earn a wage while I train Certified Nurse Assistant Create your own CNA story: Take the first step in a rewarding career in healthcare As a Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA), you provide compassionate care to seniors and people with disabilities in skilled nursing facilities across California. Becoming a CNA can be your first step in a rewarding career in healthcare . America's population is aging rapidly Long-term care facilities in the US currently serve over 8.3 million residents Learn More By 2030, the number of nursing home residents in the US is expected to double Learn More With the Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP), candidates can Earn and Learn -- meaning you can start working immediately while you obtain your certification. Learn More About Long-Term Care Subscribe * indicates required First Name * Last Name * Zip Code * Email Address * SMS Phone Number Your CNA Story - By providing your phone number, you agree to receive promotional and marketing messages, notifications, and customer service communications from Your CNA Story. Message and data rates may apply. Consent is not a condition of purchase. Message frequency varies. Text HELP for help. Text STOP to cancel. See terms . Language Preference * English Español Tiếng Việt 简体中文 Select the language you prefer to be contacted in. SIGN UP TODAY Interested in learning more? Sign up here to receive information and guidance on how to create your own CNA story — via email and/or text message. Career Paths in Long Term CAre Where will your new career take you? Certified Nurse Assistant The Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) role is a vital part of senior living communities. CNAs provide hands-on compassionate care, ensuring the well-being of residents. CNAs are essential in healthcare and have opportunities for growth. Nursing Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and Registered Nurses (RNs) provide professional medical care to residents with a personalized approach. Both requre professional degrees. Administration Administrators in senior living communities are responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the facility and ensuring all state and federal regulations are met. Social Services Social services personnel work with healthcare professionals to advocate for patients, support new residents in adjusting, and provide counseling. Therapy Therapists and related staff members work one-on-one with residents to improve mobility and strength. Care Coordination Care coordination staff work with new residents and their families. Their duties include admissions and customer service. Activities Activities directors and staff add a little fun to residential life. They plan and lead fun events to keep residents engaged. Support Services It takes many hands to ensure life runs smoothly in a senior care community. Laundry, maintenance, housekeeping and dietary staff members all play vital roles. Across California, CNAs are in high demand CNAP has designed a comprehensive program tailored specifically to CNA career seekers like you. With CNAP you can create your CNA story with confidence, unlocking a world of opportunities, and paving your way to success in the healthcare industry. Becoming a CNA is easier than you think. Follow the Earn and Learn path or the Self-funded path to your new career. Choose Your Path Career Seekers Quick Links What is Long-Term Care? Learn about the various environments where CNAs care for seniors Learn more Career Paths in Long-Term Care Explore the diverse career opportunities in the dynamic field of long-term care. Career Paths in Long Term CAre

Certified Nurse AssistantThe Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA) role is a vital part of senior living communities. CNAs provide hands-on compassionate care, ensuring the well-being of residents. CNAs are essential in healthcare and have opportunities for growth.
NursingLicensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) and Registered Nurses (RNs) provide professional medical care to residents with a personalized approach. Both requre professional degrees.
AdministrationAdministrators in senior living communities are responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the facility and ensuring all state and federal regulations are met.
Social ServicesSocial services personnel work with healthcare professionals to advocate for patients, support new residents in adjusting, and provide counseling.
TherapyTherapists and related staff members work one-on-one with residents to improve mobility and strength.
Care CoordinationCare coordination staff work with new residents and their families. Their duties include admissions and customer service.
ActivitiesActivities directors and staff add a little fun to residential life. They plan and lead fun events to keep residents engaged.
Support ServicesIt takes many hands to ensure life runs smoothly in a senior care community. Laundry, maintenance, housekeeping and dietary staff members all play vital roles.
